text: kcc is a formal C17 compiler written entirely in ARM64 assembly, and set down as a single literate program using weft , a metalanguage built to be authored and read by human and AI collaborators alike. Every instruction is explained in prose before it is written in code. It checks C against the Standard, optimises it, allocates registers, and emits native machine code; it compiles itself to a byte-identical binary; and it cross-compiles to x86-64 (Linux and macOS). It builds and runs Lua, SQLite, and DOOM — and boots a Linux kernel. The whole book is the compiler (≈1000 pages): read kcc.pdf in this repository, also published on Releases , or build it yourself (see below). Learn more about Literate Driven Development at https://literatedriven.com . Everything the machine builds — the assembly modules, the verification scripts, and the Makefile itself — is generated by tangling the literate sources. You never edit generated files; you edit the book. kcc.weft master document (LaTeX preamble + @i includes) literate/ all the chapters (prose + code fragments) assets/ cover art (SVG → the PDF covers) kcc.pdf the typeset book (committed; rebuilt with `make pdf`) README.md this file LICENSE MIT The typeset book, kcc.pdf , is committed, so the repository always carries a readable copy of the current text. Rebuild it with make pdf . There is a one-time bootstrap: because the Makefile is itself tangled from the book, you generate it first, then use it. # 1. Tangle sources, scripts, and the Makefile into gen/ (and ./Makefile). weft -p gen/ --mkdirs kcc.weft # 2. Build the compiler (gen/kcc). make # 3. Compile something with it. ./gen/kcc gen/hello.c -o gen/hello && ./gen/hello -p gen/ prepends gen/ to every tangle output; --mkdirs creates the directories. The generated tree lives entirely under gen/ (plus the root Makefile ); make clean removes it and the command above regenerates it. The verification scripts locate their own base directory, so they work under any -p prefix. make pdf weaves the .weft sources to kcc.tex and typesets kcc.pdf with LuaLaTeX. The covers are regenerated from assets/*.svg when rsvg-convert is available. The resulting kcc.pdf is committed alongside the sources, so the book can be read straight from the repository; tagged versions are also published as a Release asset on GitLab. MIT — see LICENSE .
